headline: Nvidia Beats but Momentum Stalls: Is AI Fatigue Setting In?
body:
Nvidia (NVDA) delivered Q4 FY2026 earnings beat with $1.62 EPS and $68.13B revenue (+73% YoY), powered by 91% data center mix. The stock rose 2% after-hours but premarket gains faded, raising questions about AI sustainability.

Despite strong numbers, futures indicate caution. Analysts note elevated valuations leave little margin for error. The 'buy the rumor, sell the news' pattern may be emerging after a substantial run-up.

Key question: Can NVDA maintain hypergrowth as hyperscaler capex scrutiny intensifies? Guidance will be pivotal. The modest premarket gain suggests markets may be pricing in a plateau rather than acceleration.

headline: Axon Rallies 20% as AI Drives 40% Software Growth Despite Sector Fears
body:
Axon Enterprise (AXON) defied the software sector malaise, jumping 20% after Q4 earnings beat and revealing its software business grew 40% annually, powered by AI product adoption. The stock had slid 25% in 2026 amid broader AI disruption fears.

CEO Rick Smith emphasizes AI creates defensible value: 'Our customers simply cannot replicate this.' Axon's integrated hardware-software ecosystem and real-time data moat challenge the narrative that AI universally undermines software business models.

The rally signals market discrimination between AI threats and AI opportunities. Vertical integration with proprietary data may be the key differentiator. Watch for continued software margin expansion.

headline: Oracle Jumps 4% as Oppenheimer Upgrades to Outperform on AI Infrastructure
body:
Oracle (ORCL) surged 4% after Oppenheimer upgraded shares to 'Outperform,' citing strong positioning in AI infrastructure and favorable risk-reward following recent weakness. The upgrade underscores investor appetite for AI enablers with tangible monetization.

Oracle's multi-cloud AI database partnerships position it as a key beneficiary of enterprise AI adoption. Unlike pure-play infrastructure, Oracle brings enterprise relationships and recurring revenue visibility.

The upgrade fuels broader software sector optimism after last week's AI-driven selloff. ORCL's rally signals that AI infrastructure monetization is gaining recognition as a durable growth vector, not just hype.

headline: Trade Desk Plummets 16% Despite Earnings Beat - What Gives?
body:
The Trade Desk (TTD) reported an earnings beat but saw its stock drop over 16% in premarket trading—a puzzling reaction that highlights market sensitivity to guidance and near-term expectations.

While exact reasons await analyst commentary, the sharp reversal suggests investors are focusing on deceleration signals, margin compression fears, or competitive pressures in the ad-tech space. The stock had rallied significantly into the print, making it vulnerable to 'sell the news' flows.

TTD's sell-off contrasts with NVDA's muted gain, indicating that even quality AI-exposed names aren't immune to scrutiny. Execution consistency and revenue sustainability remain paramount in this environment.

headline: PAR Technology Reports Q4 Loss Amid Restaurant Tech Headwinds
body: PAR Technology is projected to report a fourth-quarter loss of $0.02 per share on revenue of $115.71 million, according to analyst estimates. The restaurant technology provider faces ongoing challenges in the hospitality sector as consumer spending patterns shift. The company's cloud-based solutions for restaurant operations continue to gain traction, but near-term profitability remains pressured by macroeconomic uncertainty and competitive pricing in the point-of-sale market. Investors will watch for commentary on 2026 outlook and cost control measures.

headline: D-MARKET Reports Q4 Results as Turkish E-Commerce Faces Headwinds
body: D-MARKET Electronic is scheduled to report fourth-quarter earnings, providing insight into Turkish e-commerce performance amid regional economic challenges. The company, which operates the Hepsiburada platform, faces pressure from inflation and currency volatility in its core markets. Investors will focus on gross merchandise value trends, active customer metrics, and the company's ability to maintain profitability while expanding its logistics network. The results will offer perspective on emerging market e-commerce resilience compared to developed market peers.

headline: Stellantis Braces for $26B Loss as EV Transition Bears Down
body:
Stellantis (STLA) is preparing to report what sources describe as its first annual loss—approximately $26 billion—a staggering figure that underscores the auto sector's EV transition challenges. The looming loss has European markets on edge.

The magnitude reflects massive investments in electrification and softening demand for combustion vehicles. Stellantis faces dual pressure: legacy business erosion and expensive EV ramp-up.

This serves as a cautionary tale for automakers: EV transition requires enormous capital with uncertain payback. Parts suppliers and battery makers may face similar headwinds if adoption slows. Sector profitability remains under pressure.

headline: Dell Earnings in Focus: Will AI Server Demand Sustain After Nvidia's Beat?
body:
Dell Technologies (DELL) reports earnings today before the bell, with investors scrutinizing AI server demand trends following Nvidia's strong but not explosive results. Dell is a key bellwether for enterprise AI infrastructure spending.

Given Nvidia's muted premarket gain despite a beat, expectations for Dell are tempered. Markets will look for order book growth, margin trends, and commentary on hyperscaler vs. enterprise demand bifurcation.

CoreWeave (CRWV) also reports after the close, offering another lens on AI infrastructure. Diversification across vendor ecosystems will be in focus.

Watch Dell's data center segment growth and AI-optimized product pipeline updates.
